claims.text: The pooled mean prevalence of NAFLD in children from general population studies is 7.6% (95% CI: 5.5% to 10.3%).
The pooled mean prevalence of NAFLD in children attending child obesity clinics is 34.2% (95% CI: 27.8% to 41.2%).
Prevalence of NAFLD in children and adolescents is generally higher in males compared with females.
Prevalence of NAFLD in children and adolescents increases incrementally with greater BMI.
Estimated NAFLD prevalence in clinical population studies varies by region, with the highest prevalence observed in Asia.
There is no evidence that NAFLD prevalence in children and adolescents has changed over time.
NAFLD prevalence estimates in obese children and adolescents are substantially lower when elevated ALT is used as the diagnostic criterion compared to biopsies, ultrasound, or MRI.

Prevalence estimates in studies of children/adolescents attending obesity clinics and in obese children/adolescents from the general population were substantially lower when elevated alanine aminotransferase (ALT) was used to assess NAFLD compared with biopsies, ultrasound scan (USS) or magnetic resonance imaging (MRI).

methodologies.name: Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
methodologies.description: A systematic review and meta-analysis of all studies reporting prevalence of NAFLD using any diagnostic method in young people aged 1-19 years.
conditions: Any diagnostic method for NAFLD (ALT, USS, MRI, biopsy)

limitations.text: Prior narrative reviews quoted wide-ranging general population prevalences (9% to 37%) without systematic review methodology.
There was marked heterogeneity between studies in both general population and clinical population analyses (I2 = 98%).
